propositions: The autouse _no_repo_commits guard invokes git rev-parse HEAD before and after each test, creating 26k+ subprocess launches across the 13.2k-test suite and consuming ~207 runner-seconds / ~75s wall-time on macOS.
Measured A-B-B-A timing on 895 tests showed ~5s median savings (9.3%) when the guard was bypassed, projecting ~75s full-suite wall-time reduction.

The per-test contract requires detecting checkout HEAD moves, naming the responsible test, supporting allow_repo_writes escape, and maintaining the session dirty-tree backstop; eliminating subprocesses while preserving this attribution contract has no consensus-backed safe implementation.

Four surveyed OSS projects (pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit) universally avoid per-test source-checkout Git subprocess launches, but none maintains rebar's stricter per-test checkout-attribution guard, making direct primitive consensus unavailable.

Adding a Git library dependency, hand-parsing ref/storage formats, or removing the attribution guard each violates either install/dependency risk, correctness/maintenance risk, or test-fidelity constraints respectively.
